messages: A batch can affect up to 5,000 photos, including linked companions. Removing a hierarchical keyword removes that exact path, not every descendant. The keyword tree and suggestions use terms already in the catalog.
A photo in this keyword change is no longer available
A photo would exceed the limit of 100 keywords
A selected photo is no longer in the catalog

A smart collection finds photos that match its saved rules. Supported rules include flag, rating, Unrated only, file types, color label, edit status, virtual copies, and search text. Camera, lens, hierarchical keyword, capture date, ISO, focal length, aperture, and shutter-time ranges are also saved.
Add or remove keywords on a selection
Add to photo and Enter affect the active photo. The separate selection buttons act on the selected grid photos. Link pair metadata can also update their RAW or JPEG companions.
Another application changed the XMP file. Retry to merge its latest changes.

Ask the other editor to save its metadata to adjacent XMP files, then choose Local ••• → Import sidecars…. The action reads the catalog’s originals, including all pages of large libraries up to 100,000 photos per import. Virtual copies keep their own metadata.
Capture date start must not follow end.

Capture dates include both the first and last day. These filters combine with ratings and other choices, survive a reload, and can be saved in a smart collection. Existing photos gain exposure values when their source is next scanned; rescan a folder if values are missing.
Choose add, remove, or undo keywords
Enter one or more keywords, then choose Add to selection or Remove from selection. Each photo keeps its other keywords.
Expand Camera, exposure & date in Filter. Camera and Lens match part of a name. Keyword matches a complete catalog keyword path and its descendants; for example, Places includes Places > Boston.
Exposure accepts fractions such as 1/250. Set both limits to the same value for an exact match.
External XMP changes conflict with pending edits ({properties}). Read the sidecar metadata before syncing again.

Files & Metadata controls portable LightTable edits beside originals, automatic XMP writing, RAW/JPEG pairing, and keyword entry. Complete portable edits use .lighttable-state.json; XMP carries compatible edits and metadata. XMP sync preserves unrelated fields and reports conflicting external changes; read Exchange metadata through XMP sidecars for the supported workflow.
Filter camera, exposure, and capture date

For four-star photos taken at 50mm in 2026, set Rating to 4 stars and up, focal length minimum and maximum to 50, and capture dates from January 1 through December 31, 2026. Save those filters as a smart collection.

ISO, focal length in millimeters, aperture f-number, and shutter time accept minimum and maximum values. Enter the same number at both ends for an exact match. Shutter time accepts seconds or a fraction such as 1/250. Photos without the required exposure metadata do not match.

If another application changes the same XMP property after the last read or sync, LightTable reports a conflict and leaves that sidecar unchanged. Review the external metadata, then import sidecars to accept those metadata values before making further changes in LightTable.
Import at most 100000 photos at once
Import at most 100000 photos at once; narrow the source or folder scope
Keywords changed after this batch. Review the photos before undoing.
Missing exposure metadata does not match an exposure filter. Rescan folders to index existing photos.
Multiple XMP sidecars exist for this photo. Keep one naming convention before syncing.
Narrow photos by text, camera, lens, exposure, capture date, keywords, and culling marks.
Open Info beside either grid to view metadata or tag selected photos. The grid narrows to make room for the inspector. Choose another inspector tool to return to the wider grid.

Open Info on the active photo. Enter keywords in Add keywords and click Add to photo or press Enter. Commas separate keywords; Settings → Files & Metadata can also enable semicolon separators and catalog keyword suggestions.
Original is unavailable. Reconnect its folder and retry.
Read culling metadata from other editors and keep supported changes beside your originals.
Save pending edits before changing keywords
Select no more than 5000 photos for a keyword batch
Select photos and enter keywords first
Select photos in a grid to tag them together.
Select photos in either grid and open Info. Check the selected-photo count below the keyword buttons.

Supported metadata includes star ratings, pick/reject marks, standard color labels, flat and hierarchical keywords, and descriptive IPTC fields. An explicit empty value clears that field; an absent value leaves it unchanged. Custom color labels that do not match a LightTable color are reported as skipped.
That keyword change is no longer available to undo
The XMP sidecar was created, removed, or renamed by another application. Read its metadata before syncing again.

The importer reads supported Photo Mechanic and digiKam metadata conventions. Each application has additional conventions, so review a small sample in both applications before exchanging a whole library. Develop settings and crop are not applied by this menu action.

Turn on automatic XMP writing in Settings → Files & Metadata. LightTable queues changed fields and writes them beside available originals. It preserves unrelated metadata and saves a backup of the existing sidecar before first updating it. Offline or failed writes stay queued for retry.

Use Undo keyword change to restore the last batch while this window remains open. Undo refuses to overwrite keywords changed after that batch. Photo History also retains the before and after keyword states.
Use either photo.xmp or photo.RAW.xmp for one original. If both are present, import and sync report the ambiguity instead of choosing one. Keep one naming convention after checking their contents.

XMP exchanges supported metadata; it is not a complete catalog backup. Keep catalog backups for collections, history, and variants, and enable portable LightTable edits when you need the full editing recipe to travel with a folder.
